history.summary: Bhootnath Temple is a 16th-century Shikhara-style Shiva temple in the heart of Mandi town. Sources agree it was built by Raja Ajber (Ajbar) Sen, founder of the Mandi capital, but date it 1526 AD or 1527 CE (unresolved). Legend says a cow kept showering milk at a forest spot; Shiva appeared in the king's dream, directing him to dig there, where a swayambhu (self-manifested) Shivalinga was found and enshrined. The temple's construction coincided with Raja Ajber Sen shifting his capital from Bhiuli to Mandi, and he started the Mandi Shivaratri observance here. Features a gold-plated kalasha, a large Nandi facing the sanctum, and paintings/niches of deities. The CSV spelling 'Bhutnath' is corrected to the documented 'Bhootnath'. town_description: Mandi is a historic town on the Beas River and the headquarters of Mandi district, Himachal Pradesh. Known as 'Chhoti Kashi' (Varanasi of the Hills), it hosts some 81 old temples and is the venue of the famous Mandi Shivaratri Fair.

travel.railway: Joginder Nagar (narrow gauge) and Shimla (narrow gauge); broad-gauge connections at Chandigarh/Kalka
travel.road: Well connected by road to Shimla, Chandigarh, Pathankot and Delhi; temple is in the town centre

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivaratri (February/March) for the Mandi Shivaratri Fair
